hints: A Gray code lists all n-bit values, with neighboring values differing in one bit.
Build codes for n bits from the n-1-bit list: first prefix 0 in normal order, then prefix 1 in reverse order.
This reflection makes the boundary pair differ in just the prefixed bit.
analogy: Fold a list back on itself and label the two halves 0 and 1.
example: For n=2, one-bit list 0,1 becomes 00,01 then reversed with 1 prefix: 11,10.
algorithm: Start with [0]. At each added bit, append the old list prefixed by 0, then the old list in reverse prefixed by 1.
correctness: Within each half, the old one-bit-difference property remains; at the join, the reversed order makes the suffix equal and only the prefix bit changes.
complexity: O(n*2^n) time and O(2^n) output space, where n is the code length.
